observations: Photo 0: Lens barrel with focus distance/zoom scale marked 500, 400, 300, 200 and a zoom lock/unlock switch.
Photo 0: Partial branding visible - 'APO' badge, 'EX' lettering, and a fragment of '50-5...mm' text, consistent with a Sigma 50-500mm APO EX series lens.
Photo 0: Textured rubber zoom/focus rings, matte black finish, no visible cracks or dents on the barrel.

Photo 1: Rear mount shows a metal bayonet ring, an aperture scale (22,16,11,8,5.6,4), a CPU contact strip, and a small red alignment dot - consistent with a Nikon F-mount AF lens with an aperture ring.
Photo 1: Rear glass element is visible with a faint colored reflection (coating), no visible dust/fungus but resolution is too low to be conclusive.
No front element photo, no photo of the lens mounted on a camera, no video of zoom/focus/AF operation, no serial number or full model engraving visible.
A semi-transparent 'MASOGNE PROFESSIONAL' watermark overlays both images, obscuring some printed text on the barrel.

claims.claim: Sigma APO 50-500mm f/4-6.3 HSM EX DG
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'APO', 'EX', and partial '50-5...mm' text matching the claim, but full model engraving (including 'HSM', 'DG', f-stop range, and 'Sigma' brand name) is not clearly legible due to watermark and angle.
Photo 1 shows a mount style (aperture ring, CPU contacts) consistent with Nikon F-mount AF-D lenses, but no 'Nikon' or mount-specific engraving is visible to confirm.
Authenticity cannot be confirmed from photos alone; would require serial number check or close-up of engraved nameplate.
Internal motor function cannot be seen in static photos; no AF-in-action video or camera-mounted test shown.

risks.risk: Fungus, haze, or scratches inside the optical elements
risks.proof: A photo of the front element and a photo shining a light through the lens from both ends
risks.if_unproven: priced as having optical defects (worst case)

risks.proof: A short video of the lens autofocusing on a camera body
A video of the aperture ring being turned while lever is actuated, showing blades opening/closing smoothly
risks.if_unproven: priced as having aperture mechanism issues

risks.risk: Zoom ring creep or stiffness (common in old 50-500 'Bigma' lenses)
risks.proof: A video of the zoom ring being extended/retracted at various angles
A close-up, well-lit photo of the full mount ring and contact pins
risks.if_unproven: priced as mount in unknown/worn condition

risks.risk: Missing accessories (lens caps, hood, tripod collar, case) not shown
risks.proof: A photo of all included accessories laid out together

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit photo of the full lens barrel showing complete engraved model text and serial number
Video of the lens mounted on a Nikon camera body showing autofocus and image stabilization (if any) in action
Photo of the front element with a light shone through to check for fungus/haze/scratches
Video of zoom ring extension/retraction and aperture blade movement
Photo of all included accessories (caps, hood, case, collar)
response.reason: The lens type, brand, and approximate model are reasonably identified from partial markings and mount style, but optical condition, autofocus function, and full authenticity cannot be confirmed from the two photos, so it must be priced at worst case pending further proof.
